parsed.why: No trans criminal offence and working courts, but documented tier-1 exposures: facility bans across many states with an arrest, visa-screening refusals and fraud risk on document mismatch, birth-sex custody and HRT-stripping. Retrogression ongoing; remedies partial.

Statute grants self-ID and X markers, but implementation failure: patterned lethal violence against trans women, police ridicule, a ward-dispute death, weak custody safeguards. Religious court strikes self-ID. Sodomy law secondary, male-focused.

Nothing in criminal law reaches trans people; no prison system, so no placement risk. Institutional doctrine opposes 'gender theory' but binds its own institutions, not visitors. No documented trans-visitor harm; consular and factional negatives. Thin data.

Decriminalised, constitutional gender-identity protection, accepted fa'afafine tradition, conversion-therapy ban. But conservative society, police distrust discouraging reporting, one documented 2018 trans killing; no rate; no LGR (resident gap only).

No criminalisation of expression; no trans-specific violence documented. Negatives largely resident-facing (marker changes all rejected) plus documented frontier document mismatch; facilities rule an open question in a conservative but unhostile society. Thin data.
